recaps.transcript: I saw Priya this morning, third session. She came in and immediately started apologising for being late, which, she wasn't really late, like two minutes. We spent most of the time on this thing with her sister - the sister's moving to Auckland in March and Priya keeps saying she's fine about it, totally fine, but then she described this thing where she keeps re-reading the sister's old texts at midnight, which, hmm. My hunch is the worry isn't really about the move at all, it's about what happens to her role in the family when the sister goes - she's been the one who organises everything, the appointments, the birthdays. She said work's been a lot but didn't elaborate, you know, kind of deflected. She did sleep better this week, five or six hours instead of three. Next time I want to stay with the midnight texts and see where it goes. Also I was slightly distracted because my own week was heavy, I'll note that.

recaps.transcript: I met with Daniel, second time since his father died in June. I asked how the week had been and he said flat, just flat, that's the word he used. We sat with that for a while, I didn't rush it. He mentioned his brother wants to sell the house by autumn and Daniel isn't ready, he got tearful and then made a joke about it, which I let stand. I did check in about risk, because he'd looked so depleted, and he was clear with me: no thoughts of hurting himself, nothing like that, and I believed him. We talked about maybe writing the voicemail down, transcribing it, as a way to keep it without the pressure of the phone. My hunch is the house fight is standing in for the grief itself - easier to be angry at the brother than at the fact that his dad is gone. I'll come back to that gently.

I asked what stopped her and she said her niece's birthday, the party is Saturday, and she's promised to make the cake. We talked about the niece's party for a while after, the cake, the icing, and I think that was the right move, staying with the cake, the ordinary thing. My hunch is the driving work and that thought are the same conversation and I need support to hold both. recaps.transcript: Final session before a break with Tessa, and we spent it, of all things, on her son's football. Theo, fourteen, made the county squad and Tessa is, her word, unmoored, because for ten years her life was his training schedule and now he has a coach and a lift share and doesn't need her driving. She said she's happy, obviously she's happy, and then cried in the car after dropping him at practice, which, the car again, there's always a car in these. I wonder if this is less about Theo and more about who she is without the job of him, and she half-said that herself, so maybe it's not a wonder, maybe it's hers. She's also started sketching again, first time since before he was born, and she showed me one, a corner of the kitchen, and it was, honestly, good. I noticed I got a bit effusive about the sketch, which, note to self, it's not my job to be the audience. Plan: she keeps sketching over the break and we pick up the identity piece when I'm back in three weeks.
